skill.name: extract-the-hook
skill.description: Pull the openings out of posts that worked and name the shape underneath, so you reuse a pattern rather than copying a line. Use when someone wants a hook library, asks what makes an opening work, has collected posts they admire, or keeps writing the same first line. Do not reproduce anyone else's wording, and do not attach performance figures to a pattern.
skill.summary: Turn admired post openings into reusable writing patterns without copying wording or relying on unsupported performance claims.
skill.author: prateeks367

content.user_title: Extract Reusable Hooks From Proven Posts
content.value_statement: Writers often copy memorable openings without understanding why they work. This skill identifies the underlying structure and turns it into original, reusable hook patterns.
actual_capabilities: Extract the first line or two from each supplied post.
Classify openings by moves such as contradiction, confession, or direct address.
Rewrite an opening as a fillable pattern with clear slots.
Test patterns against three pieces of the user own material.
Separate reusable structure from copied wording and unsupported performance claims.
limitations: It cannot measure or predict engagement performance.
It does not rank hooks by objective quality.
It needs source openings and user material for useful pattern testing.
It does not replace subject expertise or a complete post.

use_cases.title: Build a Hook Library
use_cases.description: Turn a collection of admired openings into named patterns that can support future original posts.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Repeated Openings
use_cases.description: Compare recent introductions and identify the opening moves you repeat too often.

use_cases.title: Adapt Patterns to Your Voice
use_cases.description: Fill several hook structures with real experience, then keep only patterns that fit your subject and defensible point of view.

prompt_templates.title: Name the Hook Shape
prompt_templates.prompt: Here are six post openings. Name the move in each one without repeating the original wording, then explain the shared pattern.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of a small reference set

prompt_templates.title: Create Fillable Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these opening moves into five fillable sentence patterns. Use bracketed slots and remove every detail that belongs only to the source posts.

prompt_templates.title: Test Against My Material
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these three ideas from my work to fill the proposed patterns. Mark each result as natural, too narrow, or unsupported, and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Hook Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this hook collection. Group similar moves, remove copied phrasing, flag unsupported performance claims, and return the strongest reusable patterns with three original applications.

output_examples.input: Opening: Everyone recommends posting every day, but that advice fails for a small technical team.
output_examples.output: Move: contradiction. Pattern: [Common advice] fails when [specific group] faces [specific constraint].

output_examples.input: Opening: I spent six months redesigning our process before discovering the real bottleneck.
output_examples.output: Move: confession. Pattern: I spent [time] doing [accepted action] before learning [underlying truth].

output_examples.input: Three openings from recent posts, plus three ideas from my work.
output: Specific: [Number or concrete detail] changed how I understood [subject].
Mid-scene: [Action in progress] was when I realized [unexpected point].
Test result: The contradiction pattern fits two ideas; the direct-address pattern is too narrow for one.

best_practices: Provide only the opening lines when extracting patterns.
Test each pattern against material you can defend.
Keep structure while removing distinctive source wording.
anti_patterns: Do not copy a memorable opening and replace only its nouns.
Do not attach engagement percentages to generic patterns.
Do not judge a hook without considering the post that follows.

faq.question: What should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide six to twelve opening lines and several ideas from your own work for testing.

faq.question: Can it analyze full posts?
faq.answer: It works best with openings only, because full posts can hide the structure inside their subject matter.

faq.question: Will it copy another writer?
faq.answer: No. It extracts the underlying move and avoids reproducing distinctive source wording.

faq.question: Can it predict which hook will perform best?
faq.answer: No. It cannot measure or predict account-specific engagement.

faq.question: How many openings do I need?
faq.answer: Twelve is useful, and six is a practical minimum for comparing patterns.

faq.question: Does it write complete posts?
faq.answer: No. It creates and tests opening patterns, while you provide the subject, evidence, and rest of the post.
